title: Interior glass and mirror cleaning: squeegee sequence and streak-free finish
audience: Cleaners who clean interior windows, glazed doors, partitions and mirrors, both within easy reach and at the height where a ladder is needed.
learningOutcomes: Clean interior glass and mirrors to a streak-free, mark-free finish, using a dampen-then-squeegee method for glass and a wash-then-buff method for mirrors.
Choose the correct method and access arrangement for panes within easy reach and for panes above the height set in the business risk assessment.
Identify the products and tools that must be kept away from glass and mirror surfaces.

instruction.heading: What falls under glass in this lesson
instruction.body: The items covered are interior windows, glazed doors, flyscreens, mirrors (including bathroom and bedside mirrors) and window ledges. A pane passes only when it shows no streaks, spots, smears or prints when viewed from both sides. Frames, tracks and sills must also be dust-free and grit-free. External faces of windows may sit under a separate cleaning arrangement, which this routine standard does not set.

instruction.heading: Panes within easy reach: dampen, then squeegee
instruction.body: Begin with the upper edge of each pane and treat one pane at a time. Dampen the surface with a cloth loaded with solution, using long horizontal sweeps followed by vertical sweeps, so the pane never dries before the blade arrives. Set the squeegee at the top corner and draw it across in a single pass, then start each new pass so it slightly overlaps the one before. Clear the rubber edge of the squeegee between passes so that no grit scratches the pane. Once a pane is done, wipe the sash and sill and soak up any runoff.

instruction.heading: Panes above the height set in the business risk assessment: two people and approved access
instruction.body: Work on any pane above the height set in the business risk assessment only with approved access equipment and a second person positioned before the first move. The second person lifts the bucket and cloth up to the worker, holds the base steady and keeps people away from it. One worker climbs at any given moment. The washing and blade technique is the same as on the lower panes, but the climber stays inside the ladder's footprint and repositions the ladder rather than stretching.

instruction.heading: Mirrors: wash, then buff
instruction.body: Wash a mirror with a moistened cloth in passes that keep its reflective face wet, then buff it with a second, dry cloth. Streaks become visible when you tilt your head and view the mirror at an angle in good light, so check it that way and clear any you find. Wipe the frame too, so that dust does not transfer back onto the glass.

instruction.heading: Products to keep away from glass
instruction.body: Use a neutral glass cleaner (a neutral detergent) mixed to the strength printed on its label. Powder, paste and grit-based cleaners are not for glass or mirrors, since they scratch the surface and leave a haze behind. Solution containers stay off furniture and window sills, and any splash is mopped up before it dries into a mark.

procedure: Carry the kit to the room and choose the cloths and bucket colours assigned to that space.
Look over the pane or mirror for cracks, peeling film or other damage, and report anything you find before you begin.
Dress in the protective gear that the task and the site rules call for.
Within easy reach: wring out a loaded cloth, then wash the pane while it stays damp.
Pull the squeegee from the top corner in one movement, clear the rubber between passes, and overlap each pass.
Attend to the edges, the sash and the sill, and soak up any solution that has run down.
Look at the pane under good light and clean any streak or spot you missed.
Mirrors: wash with a moistened cloth, buff with a dry cloth, then check from an angle.
Above the height set in the business risk assessment only: fit the approved access equipment and confirm the second person is in position before any movement starts, then follow the two-person steps.
Last, take off the protective gear, put the kit away, wash your hands and log the area as complete.

workedExamples.situation: A bathroom mirror shows a dry white film after you wash it, and the cloth in your hand is now grimy.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you finish the mirror?
workedExamples.reasoning: Swap to a clean cloth, dampen it with diluted glass cleaner, and work in passes that keep the surface moist. Buff with a separate dry cloth, then check at an angle. If the film stays, report it, because it may be a surface problem that this method cannot shift. Never reach for an abrasive.

workedExamples.situation: A glazed partition rises higher than your reach, and the top band is out of reach from the floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you stand on a chair and lean across?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Use approved step ladder or ladder equipment with a second person, on a firm flat surface, and apply the one-climber rule. Avoid leaning or reaching; reposition the ladder for each new section.

equipmentAndPpe: Squeegee with a clean or replacement rubber blade
Bucket for solution, or the colour-coded bucket the site specifies
Clean cloths, disposable or reusable, plus a separate dry buffing cloth
Neutral glass cleaner, diluted as the label directs
Gloves and eye protection; a mask or hair covering where the site requires one

commonErrors.error: Running a squeegee across a pane that has already dried, which smears and scratches.
commonErrors.prevention: Re-dampen the pane before each squeegee pass.

commonErrors.error: Buffing a mirror with the cloth you just washed it with.
commonErrors.prevention: Buff with a separate dry cloth, and check at an angle.

commonErrors.error: Attacking a spot with a grit-based powder.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the approved glass cleaner, and report a spot that will not lift.

commonErrors.error: Climbing to a high pane alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the two-person method and approved access equipment for every task higher than arm's reach.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Inspect ladders before any climb: rungs, fixings and feet must be sound. Place them on level, solid footing, and open step ladders all the way. “Step ladders and ladders for interior high cleaning” sets out the full ladder rules, and “Window cleaning from the ground and with extension equipment” holds the stop-work rule.
Certain height work, including work from powered platforms, can require a licence or authorisation in particular states and territories.
The reference document mentions ladder standards in general terms only, with no standard number given.

qualityStandard: Panes show no streaks, spots, smears or prints.
Frame members, runners and ledges carry no dust, grit or marks.
Mirrors are streak-free when checked at an angle in good light.
Glass and mirrors were cleaned without grit-based powders or abrasive pads.
documentationEvidence: Area record showing the glass and mirror items completed
Defect report for cracks, film damage or any spot that will not lift
Access equipment check record for any task above the height set in the business risk assessment
summary: Within easy reach: dampen, squeegee in overlapping passes, and wipe the edges.
Higher than arm's reach: approved access, a second person, and one climber at a time.
Mirrors are washed with a moist cloth, buffed dry with a second cloth, and checked from an angle.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the squeegee pass start on wet glass?
options: Wet glass is faster to finish, so the squeegee moves more quickly.
Squeegeeing dry glass leaves streaks and drags grit across the pane.
Wet glass is the only way to see marks when you look at it from the side.

knowledgeChecks.question: A mirror has been washed, and you wiped it with the same cloth. What is the correct next step?
options: Leave it, because it is clean enough and the streaks will dry out
Buff it dry with a separate dry cloth, then inspect it at an angle.
Apply powder to lift the streak from the glass surface today

knowledgeChecks.question: The top band of a glazed partition is higher than your reach. Which approach is correct?
options: Stand on a chair and reach across to finish the top band quickly today
Use approved access equipment, a second person, and only one climber at a time.
Ask a colleague to hold a chair while you reach up to the top band of the glass.
